functional.text: add_item(product, quantity=1): add a product to the cart; adding a SKU that is already there increases its quantity.
delete_item(sku, quantity=None): remove the whole line, or decrease its quantity; deleting more than the cart holds empties the line; an unknown SKU is an error.
get_total_price(): the total after promotions, plus a breakdown (subtotal, item discounts, coupon discount).
Buy N, get M free on a SKU (e.g. 2 + 1): in every group of N + M units, M are free.
Percentage off (e.g. 10% off) a SKU or a whole category; optionally a cart-level percentage coupon.

non_functional.text: Reading the total is O(1): totals are maintained incrementally on add and delete, never recomputed on read.
Open for extension: a new promotion type is a new class; the cart is not edited.
Encapsulation: cart lines and running totals are internal; callers get read-only views and value objects.

assumptions.text: Money is integer cents in one currency; no floats anywhere.
Percentages round half up to the cent, once per line and once for the coupon.
At most one item promotion per line: if several match, the one that gives the biggest discount for the current quantity wins (no stacking); a cart coupon applies after item promotions.
The unit price is snapshotted when a SKU is first added; promotions don't change while the cart is open.
One shopper edits a cart at a time (single-threaded per cart).

out_of_scope.text: Tax, shipping, stock reservation, payment and multi-currency.
Cross-product deals (buy A get B) and fixed-amount coupons: designed for, not built.

api.notes: ValueError if quantity < 1. Re-prices only the touched line: O(k) for k promotions matching that product.
KeyError (ItemNotInCart) for an unknown SKU; quantity None or >= line quantity removes the line.
O(1): reads the running totals and applies the coupon.
Immutable value object for the checkout page.
One cart-level coupon at a time; replaces the previous one.

data.name: Product
data.why: Immutable value object (frozen dataclass): safe to share between carts.

data.name: CartLine (line item)
data.fields: product, quantity, cached subtotal_cents, cached discount_cents, matching promotions
data.why: Internal to the cart; caches its own price so a read is free.

data.name: Promotion
data.fields: BuyXGetYPromotion(sku, buy, free); PercentOffPromotion(percent, sku or category)
data.why: Strategy objects configured by the shop.

data.name: Running totals
data.why: Updated by the delta of the one line that changed.

deep_dives.title: Modelling discount types

options.name: DiscountType enum + if/elif in get_total_price
options.cons: every new promotion edits the cart; pricing logic is untestable on its own

options.name: Strategy: a Promotion interface with one class per kind
options.pros: open/closed, each rule tested alone, catalog decides which apply

deep_dives.choice: Strategy: Promotion interface with BuyXGetYPromotion and PercentOffPromotion, chosen per line by a PromotionCatalog
deep_dives.why: The cart only asks a promotion for discount_cents(unit_price, quantity); a fixed-amount or bundle promotion is a new class. Each class is a pure function of price and quantity, so it is trivially unit-tested.

deep_dives.title: Making the total cheap to read

options.name: Recompute on every read
options.pros: no cached state to get wrong
options.cons: O(lines × promotions) on every page view

options.name: Incremental running totals updated on add and delete
options.pros: get_total_price is O(1); each change re-prices one line
options.cons: must subtract the old line values before adding the new ones; needs a property test

deep_dives.choice: Incremental: each CartLine caches its subtotal and discount; on add/delete the cart subtracts the line's old values, re-prices that line and adds the new ones
deep_dives.why: Writes are rare and touch one line; reads happen on every page. A randomised test asserts running totals == full recompute after thousands of operations.

deep_dives.title: When several promotions match (stacking)

options.name: Stack all matching promotions
options.cons: order-dependent results, discounts can exceed the price, hard to explain

options.name: Best single item promotion per line, then one cart coupon
options.pros: predictable, never negative, easy to explain on the receipt
options.cons: re-evaluates k promotions when the quantity changes (k is tiny)

deep_dives.choice: No stacking on a line: pick the best item promotion for the current quantity; apply one cart-level coupon to the discounted subtotal
deep_dives.why: A 20%-off and a 2 + 1 on the same apples: at 2 apples 20% wins, at 3 the free apple wins, so the choice is re-made per change. Clear rules beat clever ones on a receipt.

deep_dives.title: Money, rounding and visibility

options.name: float prices, public fields
options.cons: 0.1 + 0.2 errors; callers can corrupt lines and totals

options.name: int cents, round half up once per line; internal state behind methods and read-only views

deep_dives.choice: Integer cents with half-up rounding; _lines and running totals are internal, lines() returns an immutable tuple of LineView
deep_dives.why: Totals must match the receipt to the cent, and only the cart may change its own state, which is what keeps the running totals correct.

wrapup.bottlenecks: None for a single cart: add/delete re-price one line (O(k) promotions), reads are O(1). Loading the promotion catalog per request is the real cost; cache it per process.
wrapup.failures: Invalid input (quantity < 1, unknown SKU) raises; the running totals are only changed through one private method so a failed operation can't leave them half-updated.
wrapup.monitoring: Log the promotion applied per line so a disputed receipt can be explained; alert when a discount exceeds a configured share of the price.
wrapup.scale: Many carts scale by keeping each cart independent (one per session) and the catalog read-only and shared.
wrapup.future: Fixed-amount coupons and buy-A-get-B bundles as new Promotion classes; a stacking policy object if marketing wants combinable deals; persist carts for logged-in users.
